newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan farmers protest at EU quotas.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan farmers protest at EU quotas.

text.p: Moroccan farmers protested on Friday at a European Union decision which they said would cut their agricultural exports of citrus and tomatoes and put them up against unfair competition.

Morocco's Citrus Farmers' Association secretary-general Ahmed Darrab said the quotas would cut to 59,923 tonnes total imports of tomatoes into the EU from a figure of 67,000 tonnes just from Morocco agreed with the EU under an association pact.
The new quota are for October 1 until December 31.
He added: "This level (59,923 tonnes) does not even correspond to that authorised for Morocco, while our country is not the only supplier for Europe.
"These new figures are incompatable with those fixed in the 'association agreement' (with Morocco)," he said, calling on the EU to open talks to resolve the problem.
Darrab also complained that new administrative regulations would put Morocco at a disadvantage with competitors, such as EU-member Spain.
Morocco sent to the EU three-quarters of its total citrus fruit exports of 625,000 tonnes in 1995, Darrab said.
The European Union earlier in 1996 sealed a trade association deal with Morocco as part of a strategy to bolster peace and stability on its southern flank.
